newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures end up on further cash strength.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures end up on further cash strength.

text.p: Reports of further cash strength added to early carryover demand and CME lumber futures moved up for the third time this week to best levels in nearly three weeks, traders said.

They said commercial buying prompted funds to continue covering short positions. Funds sold earlier in the month when cash had taken a plunge. But cash prices recovered this week and private reports put spruce in the $370 per thousand board foot-area compared with $350 last week, the lowest level since July of last year.
"Cash is looking very strong now," one trader said.
Analysts also cited concern over labor negotiations in British Columbia and forest fires in Canada as underlying supporting factors in the recent advance.
Lumber closed $6.80 per tbf higher to $2.00 lower with July up $4.60 at $385.90 and September up most at $371.00 per tbf. Only thinly traded distant months posted losses.
